findings.description: Spec explicitly requires banker's rounding (round_half_to_even) for the price-to-cents conversion. All A-outputs correctly implement banker's rounding per the EARS text. However, the real code implements half-up rounding via scaled-integer folding instead. This manifests at half-cent boundaries: the spec would round 1.005 USD to 1.00 cents (banker's rounds .5 to even), but the code rounds to 1.01 cents (half-up). Test confirms: `price_to_cents(1.005).unwrap() == Cents(1_01)`.

Code enforces rejection of zero and negative prices as DegradeReason::SubCent (line 381: `if cents <= 0`), but the spec only explicitly requires degradation for 'positive price that rounds to 0 Cents'. Spec does not address what should happen for exact 0.0 input or negative inputs. Test confirms: `price_to_cents(0.0) == Err(DegradeReason::SubCent)`. This is a code-level strengthening/boundary choice not mandated by the spec text.

A-outputs distinguish non-finite rejection in error typing (A1/A2 use InvalidPrice/anomaly; A3 doesn't explicitly specify), while code uses single DegradeReason::Permanent for both non-finite inputs and any NaN/Infinity from intermediate scaling. Spec is silent on non-finite handling; this is implicit in 'numeric USD price'.
